title: This Rat Kicks a Striking Rattlesnake in Mid-Air in 70 Milliseconds

scenes.text: This rat kicks a striking rattlesnake in the face. In mid-air.
A rattlesnake goes from frozen to bite in under 100 milliseconds. Faster than a blink.
The kangaroo rat reacts in 70. Some start jumping 38 milliseconds after the snake twitches.
Then, mid-air, it spins with its tail and slams the snake away with its back feet.
High-speed cameras caught it in the desert at night. The snakes miss again and again.
A rodent the size of your fist out-draws the fastest strike in the desert. Every night.

description:
Desert kangaroo rats dodge rattlesnake strikes that reach them in under 100 milliseconds, reacting in about 70 milliseconds, and some begin jumping just 38 milliseconds after the strike starts; a human blink takes about 150.
High-speed cameras from UC Riverside and San Diego State caught the rats reorienting in mid-air with their tails and kicking the snakes away with their hind feet.
Which animal reflex would you most want?
first_comment: The rats use their long tails to spin in mid-air, which is how they line up the kick. Rat or snake: who did you bet on before watching?
